name: Seafoam
lede: Seafoam is a brilliant yellowish green that Maerz and Paul date to 1920, and it is too bright and saturated to appear in any of our 23,781 archive paintings.

sections.title: A bright green, independently named four times
sections.body:
The ISCC-NBS 1955 census files Seafoam as a brilliant green in block 140 [1]. Maerz and Paul trace the name to 1920, on their plate 17 A 9 [1]. xkcd's 2010 color survey lists two near-identical shades, within 1.1 and 1.7 units, called *Light Blue Green* and *Light Bluish Green* [1].

ColorHub's own library places its nearest distinctly-named neighbor at [[greenish-cyan]], about 3.3 units off, with [[seafoam]] and [[baby-green]] close behind [1]. ColorHub's broader palette map also groups it loosely with [[mint]], nearly 9 units away, a looser family match than a true twin [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this bright green-mint in none of the 23,781 paintings, as photographed [2]. No museum photograph in our set carries a patch this bright and saturated across at least 5 percent of its canvas [2]. That absence is itself the finding: Seafoam, unlike the paler greens around it, reads as a modern, high-saturation color rather than a historical pigment match [2]. The absence is a property of the archive's older, varnished paintings, not proof the hue never existed [2].
